title: No clustering-only sort: an `ORDER BY` on the keys
description: DuckDB's SQL has no direction that only brings equal keys together (`ORDER BY 1 CLUSTERED` is a syntax error). A sort on the keys clusters them, at the cost of a sort.
reference: `SORT_DIRECTION_CLUSTERED` allows any order with equal keys adjacent (docs/core-semantics.md, `clustered`); a sorted order is one of them, so an `ORDER BY` on the keys refines it.

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe observations (duckdb 2.0.0, Python, macOS arm64; session duckdb-characterization-gaps)
provenance.notes: `python -m sverify_dev.probe --observations` runs each query on a fresh connection under `TimeZone = 'UTC'` (or its own setup) and records the rows as they come; `tests/test_probe.py::test_observations_are_current` checks they are current.
